title: Beckoning Cat from Right to Left
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Kogoro Mouri, Haibara, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. Unlike several other rebuilt episodes, the old lower-fidelity case file's stated culprit (Tamotsu Ishigami) matches the transcript's actual killer -- but the old file's single `e2` bludgeoning event flattens a genuinely two-attack structure that the mystery hinges on: Chika Murai struck Kanemaru with a shelf figurine (o1, right paw, non-fatal, knocks him unconscious) around 12:30-12:40pm and fled with her loan agreement; Ishigami arrived shortly before his own 1:00pm appointment, found Kanemaru conscious again, was mocked and threatened with eviction, and delivered the actual fatal second blow in the president's inner office using a beckoning cat he'd brought as a gift (o2, left paw -- the only cat in the room not part of Kanemaru's uniformly right-paw-raised collection). Ishigami then staged the scene by dragging the body to the main room to pin everything on Chika, vacuumed up blood/shards and took the dust bag, and tore out a memo page recording his own appointment. The old file also omits the brief false lead against the janitor Fumie Imaoka (accused on camera by an officer purely for being the one who found the body, before the memo evidence redirects the investigation) and the red-herring debt motives for both Imaoka and Murai. Old file's `has_motive_against` for the culprit was left as 'unspecified' -- transcript makes the motive explicit (Kanemaru was about to evict Ishigami from his cafe over unpaid debt and mocked his conciliatory gift). case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Weapon fragment under the sofa has its left paw raised, but every figurine in Kanemaru's own collection has only the right paw raised -- it came from outside, not his shelf.
Bloody pawprint on the inner office window matches the pawprint on the handkerchief used earlier to bandage Cha-Cha's paw -- proves Ishigami's cat, and so Ishigami, was in that room.
